analysis.title: Williams-Sonoma Inc. (WSM): 3Q26 top-line miss as management increases full-price selling initiatives; freight to increase costs and
key_insights: WSM closed down 15% on 11/19 versus the S&P at -2%. GS attributes the move to softer comps, possible consumer elasticity from full-price selling, higher material costs, shipping delays, and the omission of the long-term algorithm from the press release.
Management later clarified it is maintaining the long-term guide, and said the omission was meant to avoid assumptions about FY27 guidance.
GS reiterates Buy. FY27 EPS estimate falls 3.8% versus the 15% stock reaction.
3Q26 comp was +5.1% versus GS +6.4% and FactSet consensus +5.6%. Retail comp was +1.5% and e-commerce comp +6.8%. Furniture drove most of the quarter's strength.
Management cut markdowns on seasonal categories in all banners, especially Pottery Barn, and plans fewer markdowns and more full-price selling in 4Q holiday.
Pottery Barn comp was +1.8% on weaker non-furniture sales. Pottery Barn Children was +2.9%, West Elm +7.0%, Williams-Sonoma +6.8%. B2B grew 15%.

Diesel costs are about 20% higher than last quarter and could add $60mn of expense for the full year. Freight absorbed 75 bps of pressure in 3Q, partly offset by supply-chain efficiencies and lapping a shrink accrual.

Shipping delays from Middle East conflicts, typhoon season, and rail congestion at the Los Angeles and Long Beach ports could take multiple quarters to resolve. Management will pay extra to expedite deliveries.
FY26 guidance was reiterated and embeds the higher costs, with operating margin of 17.8%-18.2%.
Management expects a pipeline of newness at Pottery Barn next year with a refreshed aesthetic, including the Four Sixes Ranch collection.

The stock trades at 21.4x NTM P/E versus 3-year and 5-year averages of 19.5x and 15.7x. GS says investors need clarity on the timing and effect of the pricing initiatives and on a Pottery Barn comp improvement before turning more constructive.
GS cuts FY26 EPS to $9.54 from $9.66 and FY27/FY28 EPS to $10.48/$11.69, down 3.8%/4.4%. FY26 comp estimate falls to +6.3% from +7.0%.
The price target falls to $252 from $279, using higher relative P/E multiples of 120%/130%/140% (from 100%/110%/115%) to offset a lower market multiple of 17.3x (from 22.6x).

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after a 15% drop and cuts the target to $252 from $279. It sees intact fundamentals in the Williams-Sonoma and West Elm banners and furniture, and implies 14.2% upside.

earnings_insights: WSM 3Q26 (reported 11/19): comp sales +5.1% versus GS estimate +6.4% and FactSet consensus +5.6%. Retail comp +1.5%, e-commerce comp +6.8%.
WSM 3Q26 banner comps (reported): Pottery Barn +1.8%, Pottery Barn Children +2.9%, West Elm +7.0%, Williams-Sonoma +6.8%. B2B +15%.

WSM FY26 guidance reiterated: operating margin 17.8%-18.2%, including higher fuel and freight costs. GS estimate: FY26 EPS $9.54 (from $9.66), operating margin 18.1% (from 18.2%), comp +6.3% (from +7.0%).
GS FY27E EPS $10.48 (from $10.89) and FY28E EPS $11.69 (from $12.23), GS estimates, not company guidance.

Management did not include the long-term algorithm (mid-to-high single digit revenue growth, mid-to-high teens operating margin) in the press release outlook, and later said it still holds the long-term targets beyond 2027.
risk_factors: Inconsistent demand trends could weigh on comps, with share-of-wallet and pull-forward effects in furniture.
Margins could come under pressure once WSM stops benefiting from freight tailwinds, or if a promotional environment develops.
The stock trades above its historical average P/E at 21.4x NTM versus 19.5x (3-year) and 15.7x (5-year).
Elevated diesel costs, typhoon season, and port rail congestion could prolong shipping delays across multiple quarters.
Full-price selling initiatives could reduce volume if consumers are price elastic.
geopolitical: Conflicts in the Middle East are cited as one cause of shipping delays and higher fuel costs for WSM.

tension_points.bull_case: Management is cutting markdowns while furniture, Williams-Sonoma and West Elm comps stay strong. GS sees supply-chain efficiencies offsetting freight pressure, with product newness and B2B supporting share gains.
tension_points.bear_case: Fewer markdowns could raise consumer price elasticity and soften comps, as seen in Pottery Barn's +1.8% comp. Higher fuel costs, shipping delays, and a 21.4x P/E above historical averages add pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Pottery Barn comp that does not improve, or margin pressure once WSM stops benefiting from freight tailwinds.

theme_stances.key_argument: WSM can keep gaining share while introducing full price through collaborations, product innovation, and B2B growth.
theme_stances.evidence: they can continue to gain market share while introducing full price
